school_name: Citadel Military College of South Carolina
title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
description: Explore the unique military rituals, historic symbols, and rigorous milestones that define the cadet experience at The Citadel.

cards.title: The Silent Drill
cards.subtitle: A precision drill platoon founded in 1932
cards.notes: Watch the elite 61-member silent drill platoon perform complex maneuvers based on Prussian drills without a single spoken command.
cards.short_summary: The Summerall Guards are an elite silent precision drill platoon that performs complex maneuvers to a silent count.
cards.evidence_claim: The Summerall Guards were created in 1932 and perform unique maneuvers based on old Prussian drills that have never been written down.
cards.access_notes: Performances typically occur during Friday dress parades and special events on Summerall Field.

cards.title: The Band of Gold
cards.subtitle: A symbol of the Long Gray Line
cards.notes: Observe seniors receiving their heavy gold rings, featuring symbols like the Star of the West and the Palmetto tree.
cards.short_summary: The Citadel Ring is a highly symbolic piece of jewelry awarded to seniors who meet rigorous academic and military requirements.
cards.evidence_claim: The Citadel has only two official designed rings (cadet and non-cadet) and the presentation is a major annual milestone for the graduating class.
cards.source_title: The Ring - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The ceremony is held annually in McAlister Field House for the senior class and their families.

cards.title: The End of Knob Year
cards.subtitle: Transitioning from Knob to Cadet
cards.notes: Witness the culmination of the Fourth-Class System as freshmen complete 'The Gauntlet' and are finally called by their first names.
cards.short_summary: Recognition Day marks the official end of the highly regimented Fourth-Class System for freshmen, known as Knobs.
cards.evidence_claim: Recognition Day involves intense physical challenges followed by a formal announcement that the Fourth-Class system is no longer in effect.
cards.source_title: Recognition Day - Annual Events - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: The event takes place across campus and in the barracks; public viewing is available for the subsequent parade.

cards.title: The Long Gray Line
cards.subtitle: Weekly military review on Summerall Field
cards.notes: Attend a traditional military review featuring the entire Corps of Cadets marching in formation with the Regimental Band.
cards.short_summary: The Friday Dress Parade is a weekly public event where the Corps of Cadets demonstrates precision marching and military honors.
cards.evidence_claim: Citadel parades are held on Summerall Field most Fridays during the academic year and are free and open to the public.
cards.access_notes: Parades typically begin at 1545 (3:45 PM) on scheduled Fridays; visitors should arrive early for parking.

cards.title: The Spirit of Big Red
cards.subtitle: The official flag of the Corps of Cadets
cards.notes: Look for the red flag with a white palmetto and crescent, a historic symbol flown by cadets during the Civil War.
cards.short_summary: Big Red is the distinctive red palmetto flag that serves as the official spirit flag for The Citadel's Corps of Cadets.
cards.evidence_claim: Big Red is an official flag of the Corps, symbolizing duty and honor, and is flown at major sporting events and parades.
cards.source_title: Big Red Flag - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The flag is visible at all home football games and formal military dress parades on campus.

cards.title: The Live Mascot
cards.subtitle: A tradition of English Bulldogs since 1908
cards.notes: Meet the current live mascot, General, who lives on campus in a custom-built house and attends major college events.
cards.short_summary: The Citadel maintains a live English Bulldog mascot program, with the dogs cared for by a dedicated cadet handling team.
cards.evidence_claim: The live mascot program was formalized by the Class of 2003, and the bulldogs reside on campus in a dedicated facility.
cards.source_title: Citadel Live Mascot Team - Cadet Activities
cards.access_notes: General is often seen at Johnson Hagood Stadium during games and near McAlister Field House.

cards.title: The Best Drilled Cadet
cards.subtitle: An individual drill competition since 1886
cards.notes: Observe the annual competition where cadets compete for the prestigious medal containing wood from the historic ship.
cards.short_summary: The Star of the West is an annual individual drill competition that awards the best-drilled cadet in the Corps.
cards.evidence_claim: The competition has been a tradition since 1886 and the winner's name is inscribed on a monument on Summerall Field.
cards.source_title: Cadet Kyle O'Grady wins 2026 Star of the West competition
cards.access_notes: The competition is held annually in May on Summerall Field and is open to public spectators.

cards.title: The Doorknob Look
cards.subtitle: The signature haircut of first-year cadets
cards.notes: Learn about the 'Knob' nickname, derived from the closely shorn heads of freshmen that resemble doorknobs.
cards.short_summary: Freshmen at The Citadel are called 'Knobs' due to the mandatory short haircuts they receive upon matriculation.
cards.evidence_claim: Male fourth-class cadets receive an initial haircut at matriculation, a tradition that gives them their 'Knob' moniker.
cards.source_title: Citadel changes grooming policy to match DOD standards
cards.access_notes: Visible on all first-year cadets throughout the campus during the academic year.

cards.title: The Annual Muster
cards.subtitle: Honoring the Long Gray Line every March 20th
cards.notes: Join alumni worldwide as they gather to answer the roll call for classmates who have passed away in the previous year.
cards.short_summary: The Muster is a solemn annual tradition held on Corps Day to honor deceased alumni of The Citadel.
cards.evidence_claim: The Muster is held annually on March 20th (Corps Day) by alumni clubs worldwide to recognize fallen members of the Long Gray Line.
cards.source_title: The Citadel Muster - The Citadel Alumni Association
cards.access_notes: The main campus muster is held at the Holliday Alumni Center; other musters occur globally.

cards.title: Lights in the Chapel
cards.subtitle: A musical holiday tradition in Summerall Chapel
cards.notes: Experience a historic Charleston holiday event featuring cadet choirs and the Regimental Band in a candlelit chapel.
cards.short_summary: The Christmas Candlelight Service is a long-standing holiday tradition featuring music and scripture in the historic Summerall Chapel.
cards.evidence_claim: The service is held for three consecutive nights in December and includes a Procession of Lights by the cadets.
cards.source_title: Christmas Candlelight Services at Summerall Chapel - The Citadel
cards.access_notes: Held annually in early December; the event is open to the public but seating is limited.
